description: Na₄Mg(MoO₄)₂ is Clathrate-derived structured and crystallizes in the triclinic P1 space group. There are four inequivalent Na sites. In the first Na site, Na is bonded to four O atoms to form distorted NaO₄ trigonal pyramids that share  a cornercorner with one MgO₄ tetrahedra, corners with four MoO₄ tetrahedra, corners with four NaO₄ trigonal pyramids, and  an edgeedge with one NaO₄ trigonal pyramid. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.30-2.41 Å. In the second Na site, Na is bonded to four O atoms to form distorted NaO₄ trigonal pyramids that share  a cornercorner with one MgO₄ tetrahedra, corners with four MoO₄ tetrahedra, corners with four NaO₄ trigonal pyramids, and  an edgeedge with one NaO₄ trigonal pyramid. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.30-2.40 Å. In the third Na site, Na is bonded to four O atoms to form NaO₄ trigonal pyramids that share  a cornercorner with one MgO₄ tetrahedra, corners with four MoO₄ tetrahedra, corners with four NaO₄ trigonal pyramids, and  an edgeedge with one NaO₄ trigonal pyramid. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.30-2.44 Å. In the fourth Na site, Na is bonded to four O atoms to form NaO₄ trigonal pyramids that share  a cornercorner with one MgO₄ tetrahedra, corners with four MoO₄ tetrahedra, corners with four NaO₄ trigonal pyramids, and  an edgeedge with one NaO₄ trigonal pyramid. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.30-2.42 Å. Mg is bonded to four O atoms to form MgO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two equivalent MoO₄ tetrahedra, corners with four NaO₄ trigonal pyramids, and  an edgeedge with one MoO₄ tetrahedra. There are two shorter (1.96 Å) and two longer (2.00 Å) Mg-O bond lengths. There are two inequivalent Mo sites. In the first Mo site, Mo is bonded to four O atoms to form MoO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with eight NaO₄ trigonal pyramids and  an edgeedge with one MgO₄ tetrahedra. There are two shorter (1.84 Å) and two longer (1.92 Å) Mo-O bond lengths. In the second Mo site, Mo is bonded to four O atoms to form MoO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two equivalent MgO₄ tetrahedra and corners with eight NaO₄ trigonal pyramids. There are two shorter (1.86 Å) and two longer (1.90 Å) Mo-O bond lengths. There are eight inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded to three Na and one Mo atom to form a mixture of distorted corner and edge-sharing ONa₃Mo trigonal pyramids. In the second O site, O is bonded in a distorted trigonal non-coplanar geometry to one Na, one Mg, and one Mo atom. In the third O site, O is bonded in a distorted trigonal non-coplanar geometry to one Na, one Mg, and one Mo atom. In the fourth O site, O is bonded to three Na and one Mo atom to form a mixture of distorted corner and edge-sharing ONa₃Mo trigonal pyramids. In the fifth O site, O is bonded in a T-shaped geometry to one Na, one Mg, and one Mo atom. In the sixth O site, O is bonded to three Na and one Mo atom to form a mixture of corner and edge-sharing ONa₃Mo tetrahedra. In the seventh O site, O is bonded in a T-shaped geometry to one Na, one Mg, and one Mo atom. In the eighth O site, O is bonded to three Na and one Mo atom to form a mixture of corner and edge-sharing ONa₃Mo tetrahedra.
